news.title: Football: Soccer-FIFA must rebuild trust after scrapping World Cup investor proposal, says Boyce
news.lede: Aug 2 (Reuters) - Former FIFA vice-president Jim Boyce ⁠said on Sunday world soccer's governing body should focus on the interests of fans after President Gianni Infantino abandoned plans to sell ⁠a stake in the World Cup to private investors, calling the proposal "ludicrous". FIFA had proposed raising up to $4.2 billion by selling a ‌roughly 20% stake in a new entity that would oversee FIFA competitions, including the World Cup. The proposal, unveiled on Tuesday, drew immediate backlash. European football's governing body UEFA threatened to boycott FIFA events and accused the organisation of putting the sport's "soul" up for sale.

news.title: FIFA scrap World Cup sell-off plan after backlash
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA “will not proceed” with plans to sell stakes in a company which would run the commercial and operational aspects of its competitions, a statement from president Gianni Infantino said. The plan, which would include the men’s and women’s World Cups, has been rejected by three continental confederations with UEFA insisting its nations would boycott FIFA events.

news.title: Trump watches on as football explodes
news.lede: Being FIFA president carries an undeniable political dimension. “He looks like a prime minister,” people often say of Infantino when he appears at tournaments or FIFA Congresses. The power of the organisation he leads, and of the industry it represents, is immense. Infantino has dealt with major political figures in that sphere, from Vladimir Putin ahead of the 2018 World Cup to the Emir of Qatar and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for the 2022 and 2034 tournaments respectively.

news.title: UEFA declare loss of confidence in Infantino after World Cup sell-off controversy
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA president Gianni Infantino has “lost the confidence” of UEFA over a plan to sell stakes in a World Cup company to private investors, the European football governing body has said. Infantino announced overnight that the plan would not proceed after three confederations rejected it, with UEFA going further and saying it would boycott FIFA competitions until the proposal was scrapped.

news.title: Postman becomes 'first Englishman to hold a World Cup winner's medal in 60 years' thanks to Marc Cucurell
news.lede: Marc Cucurella may have completed one of the biggest transfers of the summer after joining Real Madrid, but it is a simple act of kindness away from the pitch that has caught the attention of football fans. The Spain defender, who helped his country lift the 2026 FIFA World Cup last month, was praised after allowing his local postman to hold and even wear his winner's medal while delivering mail to the footballer's home in Horsham, West Sussex. The wholesome interaction quickly spread across social media, with supporters applauding the defender's down-to-earth nature despite having just reached the pinnacle of international football. A memorable delivery for one lucky postman The story emerged after local postman Gary shared his experience on a Horsham community social media page.

news.title: Is Concacaf ready to make challenge to FIFA presidency?
news.lede: When news broke that FIFA was scrapping its commercialization plans, there was rampant celebration globally. Now, though, there is likely to be a fallout from the proposal and its driver, FIFA president Gianni Infantino. Within a statement released by Concacaf, it sure seems like the organization could be making a run at the throne: > Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations welcome the withdrawal of the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). > The Confederation also commends its 41 Member Associations and the wider football family for the courage and unity they have shown this week.

news.title: Opinion | A FIFA World Cup and a Village's Stolen Dream
news.lede: In the middle of the global celebration of football, when stadiums are full, screens are glowing, and millions are watching the World Cup, a small Palestinian village near Bethlehem experienced something very different.Battir lost its only football field.For most of the world, football is entertainment. In Battir, it is something else entirely—it is space, identity, and a rare place where young people can breathe beyond the pressures of daily life.The field was not a stadium. It had no grandstands, no giant screens, and no professional facilities. It was a simple community pitch.

news.title: UEFA to boycott World Cup if Infantino sell-off plan goes ahead
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. England, its fellow UEFA nations and CONCACAF have unanimously voted to boycott the upcoming men’s and women’s World Cups if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with plans to sell off shares in the tournament to private investors. UEFA’s 55 member nations held a virtual crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss Infantino’s recently announced plans to privatise and sell shares in the World Cup.
